response.title: How many solar panels do I need to refill a power station every day while boondocking in my RV for a week?
response.answer:
For a typical RV boondocking setup, you'll likely need 2–4 solar panels rated at 200W each to recharge your portable power station every day.

The exact number depends on your power station's battery capacity, how much energy you use overnight, and how much sunlight your campsite receives.

Solar panels needed by power station size

Assuming 4–5 peak sun hours per day and approximately 75% overall charging efficiency:

Power station capacity

4–5 × 200W

	

800–1,000W

These estimates assume you're replenishing most or all of the battery's capacity each day. You may need fewer panels if you only use half your battery overnight.

How much can your solar panels recharge daily?

1,000Wh battery recharge

135%

Estimated energy generated in one day, not accounting for energy used while charging.
What changes when boondocking for a week?

For seven days off-grid, I'd plan for at least 20–30% extra solar capacity to handle cloudy weather, shade, and imperfect panel positioning. Solar panels cannot guarantee a full recharge every day, especially during consecutive cloudy days.

For example, a 2,000Wh power station paired with 800W of solar is a reasonable starting point for a sunny campsite, provided the station supports that much solar input.

markup:
For a typical RV boondocking setup, you'll likely need **2–4 solar panels rated at 200W each** to recharge your portable power station every day.

The exact number depends on your power station's battery capacity, how much energy you use overnight, and how much sunlight your campsite receives.

## Solar panels needed by power station size

Assuming 4–5 peak sun hours per day and approximately 75% overall charging efficiency:

| Power station capacity | Recommended solar panels | Total solar wattage |
|---|---|---|
| 500Wh | 1 × 200W | 200W |
| 1,000Wh | 2 × 200W | 400W |
| 1,500Wh | 3 × 200W | 600W |
| 2,000Wh | 3–4 × 200W | 600–800W |
| 3,000Wh | 4–5 × 200W | 800–1,000W |

These estimates assume you're replenishing most or all of the battery's capacity each day. You may need fewer panels if you only use half your battery overnight.

## How much can your solar panels recharge daily?

{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(400)}
{@body const [sun,setSun] = DIL.useState(4.5)}
{@body const daily = Math.round(watts*sun*.75)}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <text weight="medium">Solar charging calculator</text>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Solar panel wattage</text>
    <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{watts}W</title>
  </row>
  <slider min={100} max={1200} step={100} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Peak sun hours per day</text>
    <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{sun.toFixed(1)} hours</title>
  </row>
  <slider min={2} max={7} step={0.5} value={sun} onChange={setSun}/>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="sm">Estimated daily solar recharge</text>
  <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{daily.toLocaleString()} Wh</title>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
    <row justify="between" align="center">
      <text size="sm">1,000Wh battery recharge</text>
      <text weight="medium">{Math.round(daily/1000*100)}%</text>
    </row>
    <box background="border" height="9px" radius="full" clip>
      <box background="rgba(29,133,96,0.9)" height="100%" width={`${Math.min(100,daily/1000*100)}%`} radius="full"/>
    </box>
    <caption>Estimated energy generated in one day, not accounting for energy used while charging.</caption>
  </box>
</box>

## What changes when boondocking for a week?

For seven days off-grid, I'd plan for at least 20–30% extra solar capacity to handle cloudy weather, shade, and imperfect panel positioning. Solar panels cannot guarantee a full recharge every day, especially during consecutive cloudy days.

For example, a 2,000Wh power station paired with 800W of solar is a reasonable starting point for a sunny campsite, provided the station supports that much solar input.

## Let me calculate your specific setup

{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState("2000")}
{@body const [location,setLocation] = DIL.useState("Southwest US")}
{@body const [usage,setUsage] = DIL.useState("most")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn(`Calculate how many solar panels I need for 7 days of RV boondocking. Power station capacity: ${capacity} Wh. Camping region: ${location}. Daily battery use: ${usage==="half"?"about 50%":usage==="most"?"about 80%":"about 100%"} of capacity. Include recommended panel wattage and a cloudy-weather margin.`)}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Power station battery capacity</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}>
        <radio value="1000">1,000Wh (1kWh)</radio>
        <radio value="2000">2,000Wh (2kWh)</radio>
        <radio value="3000">3,000Wh (3kWh)</radio>
        <radio value="4000">4,000Wh (4kWh)</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Where will you be camping?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={location} onChange={setLocation}>
        <radio value="Southwest US">Southwest US (Arizona, Nevada, Utah)</radio>
        <radio value="California or Texas">California / Texas</radio>
        <radio value="Pacific Northwest">Pacific Northwest</radio>
        <radio value="Other or varying locations">Other / varying locations</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>How much of your battery do you use daily?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={usage} onChange={setUsage}>
        <radio value="half">About 50%</radio>
        <radio value="most">About 80%</radio>
        <radio value="all">Nearly 100%</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button submit block>Calculate my solar panel needs <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

If you know the **brand and model of your power station** (EcoFlow, Jackery, Bluetti, Anker, etc.), share that too. Its maximum solar input can limit how many panels you can actually use.
